docs.title: 10.1.1 Syntax
docs.text: time_shift( op, period, numberPeriods, {var} )

docs.title: 10.1.2 Input Parameters
docs.text:
op: rset <*> | scal <date>

period: scal <str>

numberPeriods: scal <int>

var: scal <prop>

docs.title: 10.1.3 Output
docs.text: rset <*> | scal <date>

docs.title: 10.1.4 Semantics
docs.text: Changes the dates of the var Component of the Recordset op by adding (or subtracting) numberPeriods of the given period unit.

docs.title: 10.1.5 Additional Constraints
docs.text:
• If op is a Recordset, then

  • var must be provided,

  • must belong to the Recordset op, and

  • must be of Date type.

  • If op is a Scalar, then var must be omitted.

The period must have one of the following values:

  • A for year
  • S for semester
  • Q for quarter
  • M for month
  • W for week
  • D for day

docs.title: 10.1.6 Behaviour
docs.text: Returns a Recordset with the same data structure and number of Records as the input op. The dates for the Component var are modified by adding the numberPeriods (subtracting, if negative) of the given period unit.

docs.title: 11 Clause Operators
docs.text: Clause Operators serve to perform operations on the DPM Key Components of Recordsets. Use of clause Operators with Standard Key Components are not allowed.

docs.title: 11.1.1 Syntax
docs.text: op [where condition ]

docs.title: 11.1.2 Input Parameters
docs.text:
op: rset <*>

condition: expression <boo>

docs.title: 11.1.3 Output
docs.text: rset <*>

docs.title: 11.1.4 Semantics
docs.text: Filters a Recordset based on the value of a Key Component.

docs.title: 11.1.5 Additional Constraints
docs.text: Condition must be a Boolean expression using as input Key Components of op.

docs.title: 11.1.6 Behaviour
docs.text: Returns a Recordset with the same data structure as the input Operand, and with the Records resulting from the evaluation of the filtering condition. When the condition evaluates to true, the Record is kept, otherwise (including null), the Record is not kept.

docs.title: 11.1.7 Examples
docs.text:
Considering the following Recordset, generated from the selection {tT1, r010-020}:

refPeriod r CNT f 2022Q1 010 ES 100 2022Q1 010 PT 200 2022Q1 010 DE 300 2022Q1 010 IT 400 2022Q2 020 ES 500 2022Q2 020 PT 600 2022Q2 020 DE 700 2022Q2 020 800

{tT1, r010-020}[where CNT in {"ES", "PT"}] returns:

refPeriod r CNT f 2022Q1 010 ES 100 2022Q1 010 PT 200 2022Q2 020 ES 500 2022Q2 020 PT 600

docs.title: 11.2.1 Syntax
docs.text: op [rename compFrom to compTo {, compFrom to compTo} ]*

docs.title: 11.2.2 Input Parameters
docs.text:
op: rset <*>

compFrom: scal <prop>

compTo: scal <prop>

docs.title: 11.2.3 Output
docs.text: rset <*>

docs.title: 11.2.4 Semantics
docs.text: Changes the name of a Component.

docs.title: 11.2.5 Additional Constraints
docs.text:
compFrom must belong to op.

compFrom must be a DPM Key Component (i.e., cannot refer to row, column or sheet).

compTo name cannot be already used in op.

compTo name cannot be the name of a standard Key Component ("r", "c" or "s").

docs.title: 11.2.6 Behaviour
docs.text: Returns a Recordset with the same data structure as the input Operand, except the renamed Components, which change name. All the Records are kept.

docs.title: 11.2.7 Examples
docs.text:
Considering the following Recordset, generated from the selection {tT1, r010-020}:

refPeriod r CNT f 2022Q1 010 ES 100 2022Q1 010 PT 200 2022Q1 010 DE 300 2022Q1 010 IT 400 2022Q2 020 ES 500 2022Q2 020 PT 600 2022Q2 020 DE 700 2022Q2 020 800

{tT1, r010-020}[rename CNT to country] returns:

refPeriod r country f 2022Q1 010 ES 100 2022Q1 010 PT 200 2022Q1 010 DE 300 2022Q1 010 IT 400 2022Q2 020 ES 500 2022Q2 020 PT 600 2022Q2 020 DE 700 2022Q2 020 800

docs.title: 11.3.1 Syntax
docs.text: op [get component ]

docs.title: 11.3.2 Input Parameters
docs.text:
op: rset <*>

component: scal <prop>

docs.title: 11.3.3 Output
docs.text: rset <*>

docs.title: 11.3.4 Semantics
docs.text: Returns a Recordset where the fact is the value of one of the Key Components.

docs.title: 11.3.5 Additional Constraints
docs.text: component must belong to op.

docs.title: 11.3.6 Behaviour
docs.text:
Returns a Recordset with the same data structure as the input Operand. The Fact values the Records are substituted for the value of the selected Component.

Records with null Fact value will be omitted.

docs.title: 11.3.7 Examples
docs.text:
Considering the following Recordset, generated from the selection {tT1, r010-020}:

refPeriod r CNT f 2022Q1 010 ES 100 2022Q1 010 PT 200 2022Q1 010 DE 300 2022Q1 010 IT 400 2022Q2 020 ES 500 2022Q2 020 PT 600 2022Q2 020 DE 700 2022Q2 020 IT 800

{tT1, r010-020}[get CNT] returns:

refPeriod r CNT f 2022Q1 010 ES ES 2022Q1 010 PT PT 2022Q1 010 DE DE 2022Q1 010 IT IT 2022Q2 020 ES ES 2022Q2 020 PT PT 2022Q2 020 DE DE 2022Q2 020 IT IT

docs.title: 11.4.1 Syntax
docs.text: op [sub key_component = value {, key_component = value} ]*

docs.title: 11.4.2 Input Parameters
docs.text:
op: rset <*>

key_component: scal <prop>

value: scal <*>

docs.title: 11.4.3 Output
docs.text: rset | scal <*>

docs.title: 11.4.4 Semantics
docs.text: Filters a Recordset based on the value of a Key Component, and then drops the Key Component. If all Key Components are substituted, the result is a Scalar.

docs.title: 11.4.5 Additional Constraints
docs.text: The value needs to have the same Data type as the key_component.

docs.title: 11.4.6 Behaviour
docs.text: Returns a Recordset with the same data structure as the input Operand, except the Key Components dropped, and with the Records resulting from the evaluation of the filtering condition. When the condition evaluates to true, the Record is kept, otherwise (including null), the Record is not kept. If no Key Components remain after the substitution, the result is a Scalar.

docs.title: 11.4.7 Examples
docs.text:
Considering the following Recordset, generated from the selection {tT1, r010-020}:

refPeriod r CNT f 2022Q1 010 ES 100 2022Q1 010 PT 200 2022Q1 010 DE 300 2022Q1 010 IT 400 2022Q2 020 ES 500 2022Q2 020 PT 600 2022Q2 020 DE 700 2022Q2 020 800

{tT1, r010-020}[sub CNT = "PT"] returns:

refPeriod r f 2022Q1 010 200 2022Q2 020 600

docs.title: 12 Assignment Operators
docs.text: Assignment Operators serve to assign the result of an operation to a name or to a DPM Variable.

docs.title: 12.1.1 Syntax
docs.text: name := op

docs.title: 12.1.2 Input Parameters
docs.text:
name: the name assigned to the result

op: the operand, which can be any dpm-xl expression

docs.title: 12.1.3 Output
docs.text: Assigns the name to the op.

docs.title: 12.1.4 Semantics
docs.text: Allows a DPM-XL operation to use the result of another operation as input. By assigning a name to the result of an operation, this result can be selected using the selection operator.

docs.title: 12.1.5 Additional Constraints
docs.text: name must be a valid temporary identifier as defined in the grammar.

docs.title: 12.1.6 Behaviour
docs.text: The value of the Operand op is assigned the name name, which is non-persistent and therefore is not stored. The operand op can be obtained through an expression as complex as needed (for example: op1 := {tT1, r010-020} * 10).

docs.title: 12.2.1 Syntax
docs.text: var_sel <- op

docs.title: 12.2.2 Input Parameters
docs.text:
var_sel: a selection operator with the output variable

op: the operand, which can be any dpm-xl expression

docs.title: 12.2.3 Output
docs.text: Assigns the result of op to the var_sel.

docs.title: 12.2.4 Semantics
docs.text: Links the calculation of a DPM Variable to an expression.

docs.title: 12.2.5 Additional Constraints
docs.text: var_sel is a selection Operator that refers to a Variable or set of Variables that are defined in the DPM. The resulting Structure in op needs to be equal to the Structure of var_sel.

docs.title: 12.2.6 Behaviour
docs.text: The value of the Operand op is assigned the Variables selected in var_sel, with the objective of storing the result. The operand op can be obtained through an expression as complex as needed (for example: {tOT1, r010-020} <- {tT1, r010-020} * 10).
